text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with them through prompts, and good prompt engineering can improve the results. LLMs are very useful for writing, translating and answering questions. However, they have limits. They sometimes give wrong information, and their knowledge stops at the date of their training data. They also cannot truly understand meaning the way people do.
